I am an old man now, 62 years, and I have farmed this small piece near Lilongwe my whole life. My plot is small, only a quarter hectare of maize, so I must think carefully — one bag of fertilizer is already a big cost for me. Last season I got a FISP coupon and it helped me buy one bag of NPK and a bit of urea, so if the coupon comes again this year I will use the same way. I put the maize with pigeon pea between the rows like I always do, and I spread the manure from my small goats on the plot before the rains come.

I will plant the hybrid seed again because last time the cobs were bigger than the local seed my father used, and the agro-dealer in town sells a small packet that fits my plot. I cannot afford to spray chemicals for pests — I just walk the plot and pull weeds with my wife and sometimes my son when he comes from town. I have no pump and no river close by, so I wait for the rains like everyone here. For this small plot, me and my wife can manage most of the work ourselves, but at weeding time I sometimes call one or two young men from the village for a day or two with a little money or food.
